metric_identity.metric_name: LLM API Pricing Trends — Historical and current price per million tokens across major providers, tracking the competitive race to the bottom in LLM inference pricing
metric_identity.source_report: Composite metric drawing from: (1) Epoch AI 'LLM Inference Prices Have Fallen Rapidly but Unequally Across Tasks' (March 2025), (2) Stanford HAI AI Index Report 2025, (3) IntuitionLabs LLM API Pricing Comparison 2025, (4) Wing Venture Capital 'The Plummeting Cost of Intelligence' (2025), (5) OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and DeepSeek official pricing pages
metric_identity.publication_date: March 2025 (Epoch AI); April 2025 (Stanford HAI); ongoing (provider pricing pages)
metric_identity.methodology_notes: Epoch AI tracked the API price (per million tokens, input) charged by major providers for models achieving specific benchmark scores across 6 benchmarks (MMLU, GPQA Diamond, MATH-500, MATH Level 5, HumanEval, Chatbot Arena Elo). They computed the cheapest available model meeting each performance threshold at each point in time. Provider pricing data sourced directly from official API pricing pages. IntuitionLabs compiled side-by-side pricing across tiers (budget, mid-range, premium) from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and others. Wing Venture Capital independently tracked GPT-4-equivalent performance pricing over 18 months.

metric_value.value: Key price points as of early 2026 (per million tokens, input/output): Budget tier — GPT-4o mini: $0.15/$0.60; Gemini 2.0 Flash: $0.30/$2.50; DeepSeek R1: $0.55/$2.19; Grok 4 Fast: $0.20/$0.50. Mid tier — GPT-4o: $2.50/$10.00; Claude Sonnet 4.5: $3.00/$15.00; Gemini 2.0 Pro: varies. Premium tier — GPT-4 Turbo: $10.00/$30.00; Claude Opus 4.5: $5.00/$25.00 (down from $15/$75 for Opus 4.1, a 67% reduction). Historical reference points: GPT-3.5-equivalent performance cost $20.00/M tokens in Nov 2022 and $0.07/M tokens by Oct 2024 (280x decline). GPT-4 at launch (Mar 2023): $30.00/$60.00 per million tokens. Wing VC tracked GPT-4-equivalent intelligence falling from $180/M tokens to under $1/M tokens in 18 months (240x decline).
metric_value.geographic_scope: Global (API pricing is generally uniform worldwide, though some providers offer regional pricing)
metric_value.comparison_baseline: November 2022: GPT-3.5 Turbo at $20.00 per million input tokens (the only available model at GPT-3.5 performance level). March 2023: GPT-4 at $30.00/$60.00 per million tokens. These represent the starting points for the current price collapse.
metric_value.market_layer: platform (API pricing sits at the platform layer, directly affecting application-layer economics)

trend.year_over_year_change: Epoch AI finds prices declining between 9x and 900x per year depending on task and performance threshold, with a median of ~50x per year across all benchmarks. Specific examples: GPT-3.5-level inference (MMLU 64.8%): from $20.00 to $0.07 in 18 months (280x). GPT-4-level on PhD science questions (GPQA Diamond): 40x per year decline. OpenAI specifically: GPT-4o mini (Jul 2024) was 60% cheaper than GPT-3.5 Turbo while being more capable. Anthropic: Opus 4.5 priced at 67% less than Opus 4.1 ($5/$25 vs $15/$75). The budget model tier (sub-$1/M tokens) barely existed before mid-2024 and now includes offerings from every major provider.
trend.compound_annual_growth_rate: Median price decline of ~50x per year implies a negative CAGR of approximately -98% annually for fixed-performance inference. For the specific GPT-3.5-level inference: -99.6% over 18 months (Nov 2022 to Oct 2024).
trend.forecast_value: If the median 50x/year decline continues, GPT-4-level inference could cost under $0.01 per million tokens by late 2026 or early 2027. Epoch AI notes the fastest decline rates (900x/year) emerged only after January 2024 and may not persist. Industry consensus suggests inference costs approach near-zero for commodity tasks by 2027, with premium pricing persisting only for frontier reasoning capabilities.
trend.velocity_indicator: cost_halving_time: At the median 50x/year decline rate, prices halve approximately every 2-3 months. For hard coding tasks specifically, inference costs halve roughly every 2 months. The budget tier (sub-$1/M tokens) went from nonexistent to containing 5+ competitive models in under 18 months (mid-2024 to early 2026).

entrepreneurial_relevance.relevance_for_entrepreneurs: LLM API pricing is the single most important cost variable for any AI-powered startup. The implications are profound: (1) The 'race to the bottom' in API pricing means that startups building thin wrappers around LLM APIs face severe margin compression — if your product's value is primarily 'access to an LLM,' you are competing with providers who are willing to price at or below cost to gain market share (Google subsidizing Gemini across 1.5B Search users, DeepSeek pricing 90% below Western competitors); (2) The emergence of sub-$1/M token models (GPT-4o mini, Gemini Flash, DeepSeek) makes AI-powered features economically viable for high-volume, low-margin applications (customer support, content moderation, document processing) that were previously cost-prohibitive; (3) The 67% price drop in Claude Opus 4.5 vs 4.1 shows that even premium-tier pricing is falling fast — do not build business models that assume current premium pricing persists; (4) For French/European startups, Mistral AI's open-weight models offer a local alternative with competitive pricing and EU data sovereignty advantages; (5) The pricing divergence between providers creates arbitrage opportunities — smart routing between models based on task complexity can reduce costs 5-10x versus using a single provider; (6) Chinese providers (DeepSeek, Qwen) entering with dramatically lower prices forces global providers to compete, accelerating the decline for everyone.
entrepreneurial_relevance.actionable_insight: Build multi-model architectures from day one: route simple tasks to budget models ($0.15-0.50/M tokens) and complex reasoning to premium models ($3-15/M tokens). This 'model routing' approach can reduce average inference costs by 5-10x. Do not sign long-term volume commitments at current prices — negotiate shorter terms with price adjustment clauses. Budget for AI costs declining ~50% every 3 months when doing financial projections. Explore open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek) for self-hosting, as the cost crossover where self-hosting beats API pricing is moving earlier with every model generation.

confidence.cross_reference: Epoch AI analysis (https://epoch.ai/data-insights/llm-inference-price-trends) corroborated by Stanford HAI AI Index 2025 (https://hai.stanford.edu/ai-index/2025-ai-index-report), Wing Venture Capital independent analysis (https://www.wing.vc/content/plummeting-cost-ai-intelligence, reports 240x for GPT-4-equivalent), IntuitionLabs pricing comparison (https://intuitionlabs.ai/articles/llm-api-pricing-comparison-2025), Vantage cost analysis (https://www.vantage.sh/blog/gpt-4o-small-vs-gemini-1-5-flash-vs-claude-3-haiku-cost), official provider pricing pages (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google). Multiple independent sources converge on the same order of magnitude for price decline rates.
confidence.caveats: API list prices do not reflect negotiated enterprise pricing, which can be 30-60% lower for high-volume customers. Prices per million tokens do not account for differences in output quality, latency, rate limits, or reliability between providers. Some providers (notably Google with Gemini) may be pricing below cost as a market share strategy, which is not sustainable indefinitely. Chinese provider pricing (DeepSeek) may reflect different labor costs and regulatory environments rather than pure technical efficiency. The 9x-900x/year range is extremely wide, and the 900x figure comes from a short time window (post-Jan 2024) that may represent a one-time adjustment rather than a sustained trend. Token-based pricing does not capture the full cost of using LLMs (engineering time, evaluation, guardrails, monitoring). Multimodal pricing (images, audio, video) follows different and less dramatic decline curves.
confidence.measurement_reliability: verified_financial_filing (API prices are publicly posted by providers and directly verifiable; Epoch AI analysis uses systematic benchmark-to-price tracking; decline rates are computed from observed market prices, not estimates)
